examples.trans: I knew it would rain.
Do you know how to swim?

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.

examples.text: 진짜 이럴 줄 알았으면 할부하지 말고 일시불 했어야 되는데. 이제 깔끔하게 끝난 거다, 계산!

meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: I contacted them. But there is no reply.

examples.text: 너 혜주 좋아하지? 하늘이 무너지는 표정을 짓더라.

This is my first time coming to Seoul.

examples.trans: He tries hard not to let it show, but feelings like that always show.

examples.trans: She tries hard not to show it, yet I think I understand that feeling a little.

meanings.note: Native Korean expression of thanks; 고마워요 is warm and polite.

examples.trans: If you wish for it, you have to make an effort and express it—then your heart might just reach the other person.

examples.text: 나를 위해서 태어나서 처음으로 있는 힘을 다해서 용기 내줘서 고마워, 마음 표현해줘서 고마워. 나는 내가 굉장히 가치 있는 사람이라고 느꼈어.
examples.trans: Thank you for summoning every ounce of courage for me and expressing your heart—because someone as wonderful as you did that, I felt like a truly valuable person.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 설령 조금 취했다 해도 술버릇이 굉장히 깔끔한 편이라.
examples.trans: Even supposing I do get slightly tipsy, my drinking habits are remarkably neat.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (가치를).

examples.trans: Viewed positively, a preemption can be another chance to prove how valuable our show really is!

examples.trans: The longer a show runs, the more viewers take it for granted—only when it is gone do people realize how precious it is!

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

examples.text: 지난번도 느낀 건데 너 누구한테 연애를 가르치니?
examples.trans: I noticed this last time too—who do you think you are lecturing about romance?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 느끼다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (felt, noticed).

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e (나중에).

examples.trans: See you later.

examples.text: 당연해 그건. 점심 먹어야지. 여기서 군만두 맛있어.
examples.trans: Of course you won't. Let's eat lunch. The fried dumplings here are delicious.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.

examples.trans: Feeling sorry at first can eventually feel natural—my feelings toward you, and my standing right beside you, could come to feel natural too.

examples.text: 이번에는 꼭 제대로 해 보고 싶어요, 당연해지다는 마음으로요.

meanings.note: commonly used with -에 (옆에)

examples.trans: Please sit next to me.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.

examples.trans: Do you have time?

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
